_README: MARKER-ONLY. Never shipped to the student before a teacher/marker PDF is actually generated. English-only, never translated. See CLAUDE.md §5.

markingScheme.criterion: Accurately describes the pattern between angle of incidence/tilt and power output, quoting at least two of their own logged readings from the Investigation Record.
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine readings that show the trend (higher power when angle of incidence is closer to 0°/panel faces the sun more directly); exact wording not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('the power changed') with no actual readings quoted.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains the underlying scientific mechanism: a smaller angle of incidence means more sunlight energy lands per unit area of the panel's surface (concentrated vs spread-out light), which the photovoltaic cells convert into more electrical power.
markingScheme.accept: Any scientifically equivalent phrasing about light being more 'concentrated', 'direct' or 'perpendicular' producing more power; exact keywords not required.

markingScheme.criterion: States clearly whether this evidence supports or contradicts the hypothesis made in Predict, and why.
markingScheme.insufficient: Restating the hypothesis without judging it against the evidence.

markingScheme.criterion: Correctly identifies that a fixed-tilt panel's angle of incidence to the sun changes constantly through the day (large near sunrise/sunset, smallest near solar noon), while a sun-tracking panel keeps a near-0° angle of incidence all day.

Links this directly to the mechanism from Explain — a smaller angle of incidence for more of the day means more total sunlight energy captured, so the tracking panel generates more electricity over a full day.
Names both options explicitly in the comparison (fixed-tilt AND motorised tracking) and states which one wins overall, not just a single vague reason.
markingScheme.insufficient: A single vague reason ('tracking is better because it's newer technology') with no named mechanism or comparison of both options.

Clearly cites at least two specific readings from own Investigation Record, explains the angle-of-incidence mechanism correctly, and judges the result against the hypothesis — all three analytic points present.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful attempt to compare fixed-tilt and tracking panels.
States which option is better but without a named mechanism or without naming both options.
Names both options and links to the angle-of-incidence mechanism, with one gap in the reasoning chain.

Names both options, explains that tracking keeps a near-0° angle of incidence all day while fixed-tilt does not, and correctly concludes tracking captures more total energy over a full day — all three analytic points present.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across both the Explain and Apply answers together — independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks above.

levels.descriptor: Too unclear or incomplete for the reasoning to be followed reliably.
Main meaning understandable, but organisation, precision or scientific vocabulary has problems.
Clear and logical, uses appropriate scientific vocabulary (angle of incidence, photovoltaic, tilt), precise enough to follow easily.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply), using each question's point-by-point markingScheme above (award each point independently unless it states a dependsOn, in which case only award it if the point it depends on was also awarded) and the rubric's level descriptors, which restate the same points as bands — do not invent extra criteria beyond what is defined here. Each rubric row's 'source' states exactly which question's marks it equals; never award a criterion's marks a second time on top of the question-level marks they restate. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy (6 marks). Accept scientifically valid alternative wording per each point's 'accept' field; do not penalise spelling or grammar unless it actually interferes with meaning. Use the raw Investigation Record data (not just the student's summary of it) to verify any claim the student makes about their own readings. Report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 80 words.
